# 🤯 OMG — Oh My GitHub ### 🚀 One Prompt In. A Full Game or App Out. 🚀 [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-🔥%20works-brightgreen?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/denaidark/OhMyGithub?style=for-the-badge&logo=github)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/issues) [![GitHub Actions](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub%20Actions-automated-2088FF?style=for-the-badge&logo=githubactions&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![OpenCode](https://img.shields.io/badge/powered%20by-OpenCode-111111?style=for-the-badge)](https://opencode.ai/) ```text ╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗ ║ DESCRIBE IT → BUILD IT → TEST IT → PLAY IT ║ ║ ║ ║ One GitHub issue. One prompt. A complete project. ║ ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝ ``` **No API keys to configure. No server to maintain. No local setup maze.**
--- ## 🤯 What Is OMG? > **Your GitHub issue becomes the product brief.** OMG (Oh My GitHub) is an automated GitHub Actions workflow for creating complete browser games and app projects from one natural-language prompt. Write what you want in an issue and add the `OpenCode` label. OpenCode checks out the project, uses the shared skills, builds the experience, runs tests, verifies the result, and publishes an immutable OmGithub project link from the finished commit. Yes, it creates the code. Yes, it runs the verification loop. Yes, it can expose the result in a temporary browser URL. ## 🧠 TL;DR 1. Open a GitHub issue. 2. Describe the game or app you want. 3. Add the `OpenCode` label to the issue. 4. Let GitHub Actions build, test, verify, and propose the result. ```text Your idea → GitHub issue → OpenCode → tests → immutable OmGithub project ``` ## ⚡ Quick Start Create an issue in your repository with a concrete request: ```text Build a neon asteroid game. Requirements: - Arrow-key movement - Score and restart button - Win and lose states - Responsive browser layout - Run tests and verify it in a browser ``` That is the whole user-facing workflow. GitHub Actions handles the runner, OpenCode handles implementation, and the workflow handles verification plus the immutable project commit. To run against an existing non-default branch, end the issue title with a `branch: ` directive. The directive selects the checkout and is removed before the issue body is sent to OpenCode: ```sh gh issue create \ --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub \ --title "Custom branch smoke test branch: codex/omgithub-site" \ --body "Build a tiny browser page." \ --label Goal \ --label OpenCode ``` The GitHub App validates the branch before dispatching. If the directive is absent, the repository default branch remains the target. ## 🌍 What Can You Build? --- I want you to build a first-person shooter at the level of the most recent Call of Duty games. It should be utterly perfect, visually beautiful, with every single thing done at AAA quality—from textures to physics to anything you could think of. Fan out sub-agents and have sub-agents tackle each one individually so that the game is utterly perfect. Have a separate sub-agent check each item visually to ensure it looks triple A. That separate sub-agent should be a really harsh critic, and if it doesn't look triple A, keep iterating until it does. Don't stop until each sub-agent is utterly wowed with the quality when compared with the actual Call of Duty game. It should literally compare them side by side blind and say which one looks better. Do this in ThreeJS. Continue iterating until it's utterly perfect. Fan out sub-agents and ultracode.

```
generateMaze(){
 const W=this.W=21,H=21;
 const g=Array.from({length:H},()=>Array(W).fill(1));
 let x=1,y=1; g[y][x]=0; const stack=[[x,y]];
 while(stack.length){
   const [cx,cy]=stack[stack.length-1];
   const dirs=shuffle([[2,0],[-2,0],[0,2],[0,-2]]);
   let moved=false;
   for(const [dx,dy] of dirs){
     const nx=cx+dx, ny=cy+dy;
     if(nx>0&&ny>0&&nx<W-1&&ny<H-1&&g[ny][nx]===1){
       g[cy+dy/2][cx+dx/2]=0; g[ny][nx]=0; stack.push([nx,ny]); moved=true; break;
     }
   }
   if(!moved) stack.pop();
 }
 // extra loops
 for(let i=0;i<40;i++){ const x=randInt(2,W-3), y=randInt(2,H-3); if(g[y][x]===1 && ((x%2===0)!==(y%2===0))) g[y][x]=0; }
 // rooms
 for(let r=0;r<3;r++){ const cx=randInt(3,W-4), cy=randInt(3,H-4); for(let y=cy-1;y<=cy+1;y++)for(let x=cx-1;x<=cx+1;x++) if(x>0&&y>0&&x<W-1&&y<H-1) g[y][x]=0; }
```

## Objective
- Build a browser game from the user's terse prompt “Soul eyes demon” and the attached screenshot of a mobile horror game showing a skull-faced demon with glowing yellow eyes in a hospital corridor, using the OMGithub/OpenCode issue workflow.

## Requirements
- The user provided no explicit requirements beyond the phrase and screenshot; infer a first-person horror experience featuring the soul-eyed demon.
- Must be playable/responsive on Android and iOS phones/tablets with usable touch controls, safe areas, and no browser gesture conflicts (per repo conventions).
- Project must serve a static `index.html` (or Vite) and pass browser capture with auto-start.

## Decisions
- Built an original Three.js game titled **SOUL EYES** in plain static HTML/JS with vendored Three.js r161 (`vendor/three.module.js`), no external assets/network.
- Gameplay: explore a procedural hospital maze, collect 5 glowing souls, avoid a stalking demon, then escape through an unlocked EXIT gate; death jumpscare/retry, win screen, pause/restart, timer, stamina, flashlight, synthesized WebAudio.
- Start screen title/button and HUD designed to resemble the reference: pause bars top-left, SOULS pips top-center, recording-style timer top-right, joystick bottom-left, sprint/light/sound touch buttons.
- Demon starts ~6m down a guaranteed straight opening corridor, dormant for 3.8s, so the capture screenshot frames it; then it stalks/hunts via BFS pathfinding and LOS.
- `LOW_GFX` path for mobile/software renderers (`llvmpipe` detected via `WEBGL_debug_renderer_info`, plus `navigator.webdriver`): shadows off, pixel ratio 0.85, bump maps removed, fewer fixture lights/dust.
- Removed automatic pointer lock on start because it caused camera drift in Playwright mobile capture; pointer lock now only on canvas click with a 260ms `lockGuard`.
- Hidden HUD on menu/pause/death/win; hint moved above mobile controls.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented full project files: `index.html`, `css/style.css`, `js/game.js`, `js/world.js`, `js/demon.js`, `js/textures.js`, `js/audio.js`, `js/config.js`.
- Procedural textures (concrete, floor tiles, ceiling, metal, fabric, skin, robe, blood, door), props (beds, gurneys, IV stands, carts), signs, blood decals, dust, flickering fixtures, exit gate, five soul pickups.
- Demon model and AI: skull head, glowing eyes, hanging strands, robed body, arms/claws, dormant/stalk/hunt/search/scare states, catch logic, growl/audio threat.
- Verified gameplay via Playwright at 640x480: movement, all 5 soul pickups, exit activation, win screen/play again, pause/resume, death screen/retry; zero page errors.
- Fixed floating/mirrored wall signs and wall blood decals (position used `-dx` instead of `+dx`).
- Updated `README.md`? **Not yet** — original OMGithub template still present.
- Screenshots generated at `screenshots/final-desktop.png` and `screenshots/final-mobile.png`; capture strict passes.

### Active
- Visual polish of the demon face: eyes currently render as bright yellow rings/halos with dark centers (likely skull/socket geometry intersecting or eye light/glow sprite interaction), not the solid glowing orbs in the reference. Currently investigating with `/tmp/opencode/eye.mjs`; latest debug screenshots `/tmp/opencode/eye-before.png` and `/tmp/opencode/eye-magenta.png` showed the camera pointing at a wall/ceiling because debug teleport did not face the demon correctly, so diagnosis is incomplete.
- Need to re-verify final visual after any eye fixes.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Diagnose/fix the demon eye rendering so the eyeballs read as solid yellow soul-orbs (consider removing/altering the black torus rim or flattening skull surface around eyes; inspect with a correct camera teleport facing the demon).
2. Re-run `CAPTURE_URL=http://localhost:3002 CAPTURE_DIR=screenshots CAPTURE_STRICT=1 ./capture.sh` and inspect both screenshots.
3. Update `README.md` with game description/controls while preserving the `<!-- omgithub:readme:start -->` block.
4. Optionally re-run gameplay smoke test at 640x480 (`/tmp/opencode/test2.mjs`) after visual edits.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: screens, HUD, start/pause/death/win overlays, favicon.
- `css/style.css`: all layout, responsive/mobile safe-area styling, grain/vignette, menu/title design.
- `js/game.js`: renderer/quality detection, state machine, input, flashlight, loop, UI/audio wiring, debug API `window.__SOUL_EYES__`.
- `js/world.js`: maze generation, layout, spawn corridor, props, signs/decals, souls, exit gate, BFS/LOS/collision.
- `js/demon.js`: demon rig and AI; eye/socket construction around lines ~119-190; `eyeMats`, `eyeGlows`, `jawGroup`.
- `js/textures.js`: procedural canvas textures and all shared materials.
- `js/audio.js`: synthesized ambient/heartbeat/growl/scare/pickup audio.
- `js/config.js`: constants and helpers.
- `vendor/three.module.js`: vendored Three.js r161.
- `screenshots/final-desktop.png`, `screenshots/final-mobile.png`: latest capture outputs.
- `/tmp/opencode/test2.mjs`: working gameplay smoke test.
- `/tmp/opencode/capture.sh` not present; capture script is repo `capture.sh`.

## Important Context
- Dev server currently running in background on port 3002 via `PORT=3002 ./start.sh` (shell ID `sh_1929ec49e001xhZiafkOHPTZE6`); server serves static files live and is still active.
- `startForCapture` auto-clicks a single visible button whose text matches `/^(start|play)(\s+(game|now))?$/i`; the start button is labeled exactly `Start`.
- Capture uses desktop 1440x900 and mobile 390x844; screenshots show timer `00:00` because software rendering runs only ~2–3 fps and only ~1s real time passes.
- Playwright environment uses `llvmpipe`; low quality is active (`lowGfx: true`, pixel scale 0.85).
- Gameplay update `dt` is capped at 0.05, so tests on software renderer need long waits (~700ms per soul) or lower viewport.
- `world.generate()` computes `this.openCells` before carving the opening spawn corridor, so props/signs/decor do not include those extra corridor cells (acceptable but relevant).
- Demon catch radius 1.34m; player walk 3.95 m/s, sprint 6.35, demon hunt 3.92; exit requires 5 souls.
- `window.__SOUL_EYES__` exposes `state`, `world`, `demon`, `renderer`, `gpuName`, `lowGfx`, `start`, `restart`, `mode` for testing.

# SOUL EYES

A first-person browser horror game. You wake in a derelict hospital with five souls scattered through the maze. Collect all five, stay out of the demon's sight, and escape through the EXIT gate.

Everything is procedural — geometry, textures, audio, and the demon are generated at runtime with a vendored copy of Three.js. No external assets, fonts, or network requests.

<!-- omgithub:readme:start -->
## 🚀 Build, play, and remix with OMGithub

**Created using [OMGithub.com](https://omgithub.com).**

[![OMGithub](https://img.shields.io/badge/OMGithub-Open%20project-orange?style=for-the-badge)](https://omgithub.com/tomst6619-cmyk/PlayGround)
[![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source-181717?logo=github&style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/tomst6619-cmyk/PlayGround)

- 🎮 [Open the project](https://omgithub.com/tomst6619-cmyk/PlayGround).
- ✨ [Remix this project](https://omgithub.com/?remix=tomst6619-cmyk%2FPlayGround).
- 💻 [Explore the source](https://github.com/tomst6619-cmyk/PlayGround).
- 🛠️ [Check build runs](https://github.com/tomst6619-cmyk/PlayGround/actions).
- 🐛 [Report an issue](https://github.com/tomst6619-cmyk/PlayGround/issues).
- 👤 [Explore the creator's projects](https://omgithub.com/tomst6619-cmyk).
- 🌍 [Create with OMGithub](https://omgithub.com).
<!-- omgithub:readme:end -->

## How to play

1. **Find the five souls.** They glow in the dark; the pips at the top of the screen track your progress.
2. **Stay out of its sight.** The demon follows sound and line of sight. Break away, round corners, and use the flashlight sparingly.
3. **Escape.** With all five souls collected, the EXIT gate unlocks. Reach it before the demon catches you.

Getting caught triggers a jump scare and a retry. There is no penalty for taking your time — apart from the thing hunting you.

### Controls

| Action | Keyboard / mouse | Touch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Move | `WASD` / arrow keys | Left joystick |
| Look | Mouse (click the scene to lock the pointer) | Drag anywhere on the scene |
| Sprint | `Shift` (uses stamina) | `SPRINT` button |
| Flashlight | `F` | `LIGHT` button |
| Mute | `M` | `SND` button |
| Pause | `Esc` / `P` | Pause bars, top-left |

The layout respects phone safe areas and disables browser gestures on the game surface, so it plays in portrait or landscape on Android and iOS.

## Run locally

The game is plain static HTML/JS. Any static file server works:

```bash
./start.sh                 # project helper (uses PORT if set)
# or
python3 -m http.server 3002
```

Then open <http://localhost:3002/>.

For the screenshot capture smoke test:

```bash
CAPTURE_URL=http://localhost:3002 CAPTURE_DIR=screenshots CAPTURE_STRICT=1 ./capture.sh
```

## Tech notes

- Three.js r161 is vendored in `vendor/`, so the game runs offline.
- On software renderers and mobile GPUs the game detects `llvmpipe`/WebDriver, lowers the pixel ratio, disables shadows, and drops expensive texture work automatically.
- `window.__SOUL_EYES__` exposes the game state, world, demon, and renderer for debugging and automated tests.

The layout respects phone safe areas and disables browser gestures on the game surface, so it plays in portrait or landscape on Android and iOS.

## GYM SURGE bonus game

A second, lighter first-person game is included: **GYM SURGE** (`gym.html`), linked from the SOUL EYES start screen.

You are in the St. Mercy sports hall during a size-shift trial. Collect glowing energy orbs and hold the surge for 60 seconds. Sport boys shrink as the surge takes hold and burn out quickly; sport girls grow taller and hold the charge longer. If your charge empties, the outfit resets with a flash and you have to release and recharge.

- `WASD` / left joystick: move
- `Space` / `HOLD` button: surge
- Mouse drag / touch drag: look
- `Esc` / `P`: pause
- `M`: mute

Your best surge time is stored separately for the boys' and girls' trials. The background athletes run their own surge cycles so you can watch the boys burn out sooner and the girls hold the court longer.

A Toms tsi school sports experiment.
